title: Charge-Reversal-Based Extraction of Muonic Ions
authors: Song Guo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06923v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Negative muon capture in matter is accompanied by Auger electron emission and the formation of positively charged muonic ions. This charge reversal provides a possibility for electromagnetic extraction of the products of muon capture. Here we propose a charge-reversal-based extraction scheme for muonic ions, in which negative muons are moderated and confined in a dilute gas environment before conversion, and the resulting muonic ions are subsequently accelerated and extracted by electrostatic fields. The feasibility of the concept is investigated through order-of-magnitude estimates of the competing processes, including muon moderation, muonic-ion formation, charge exchange, and acceleration in the gas medium. A magnetic-electrostatic deceleration scheme is proposed to reduce the transverse phase space of practical low-energy muon beams while retaining controlled longitudinal motion, and is directly matched to the electrostatic capture region. The analysis indicates that muonic-ion formation and extraction within the muon lifetime are not excluded by fundamental timescale constraints, although the quantitative efficiency remains uncertain because several relevant low-energy cross sections and charge-state populations are poorly constrained experimentally.

title: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Tam\'as Vaszary
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06975v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation have been conjectured to offer up to a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods; however, the devil is always in the details. Here, we determine key physical conditions under which this quartic separation could be achieved in the relevant parameters. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order $m$, we find that the end-to-end speedup is of order $(m+4)/(m+1)$ in the simulation time, and $4/(m+1)$ in the accuracy, with exponential memory advantage. For elastic lattice systems, we define microscopically resolved bulk observables (MRBOs) as those that can be efficiently extracted from a quantum state, but cannot be resolved by a known continuum model with fewer degrees of freedom than the lattice. We then argue that the estimation of MRBOs is a candidate problem for quartic quantum advantage in problem size. We propose MRBOs for pseudorandom heterogeneous materials as an explicit end-to-end application where this occurs, while admitting efficient `quantum cheese' encodings of the material properties. We thus demonstrate how the interplay between regularity, physical scale, observable sensitivity and quantum encodability constrains the relation between classical and quantum complexity.

title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices
authors: Marek Rychetsky, Valentin Duruisseaux, Freya Shah, David L. Craig, Ming Ni, Georgios Katsaros, Taylor L. Patti, Anima Anandkumar, Natalia Ares
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06994v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gate-defined semiconductor quantum dots are promising building blocks for scalable spin-based quantum processors, however their operational properties depend on several fabrication and control parameters, such as lithographic gate layout and applied voltages. Existing device architectures have been refined through repeated fabrication and experimental testing, producing layouts that support reliable device operation. However, this process does not exhaustively explore the design space, limiting the ability to obtain qubits with targeted properties. We address these challenges by presenting a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and the gate electrode layout. A semiclassical Thomas--Fermi electrostatic simulator provides reference data for a Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate, which predicts the two-dimensional charge-density field. The desired spatial distribution of the confined charge defines the target quantum-dot geometry for inverse design. The FNO reproduces charge densities with a relative $L^2$ test error of just 0.6\% and enables millisecond-scale differentiable evaluations. Relative to the CPU-based physics simulator, the FNO achieves a 17,000-fold speed-up on GPU for a single design, with further performance gains enabled by batched inference. When embedded in a gradient-based design loop with fabrication constraints, the FNO can produce both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions. The ability to engineer these distinct confinement configurations demonstrates control over quantum-dot shape and position, providing a route towards designing devices with distinct qubit-relevant operating properties prior to fabrication.

title: All Bell inequalities with a quantum advantage in the minimal scenario are self-testing
authors: Mu-En Liu, Andrea Zingarofalo, Victor Barizien, Jean-Daniel Bancal
abstract:
arXiv:2611.06997v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the minimal Bell scenario, all extremal quantum correlations are known, but the Tsirelson inequalities that delimit the quantum set remain poorly understood. We study which correlations can maximize a given Tsirelson inequality, and conversely, which inequalities are maximized by a given correlation. We show that every Tsirelson inequality with quantum advantage is maximized by a single, extremal correlation, and thus self-tests the corresponding realization. This characterizes all self-tests based on linear Bell inequalities in this scenario. We also show that at most a two-dimensional family of inequalities can be maximized by a nonlocal extremal correlation. We identify these as polygons for a family of correlations realized by qubit states of arbitrary entanglement. This allows us to deduce that the quantum set is not self-dual.

title: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions
authors: Raghav G. Jha, Dengyao Luo, Alexander F. Kemper, Bojko N. Bakalov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Free-fermion states are classically simulable, yet, written as qubits, they typically carry extensive magic, the quantum resource that stabilizer circuits lack. Part of this magic is nonlocal: local unitaries acting separately on two parts of the system cannot remove it. If these local unitaries are restricted to Gaussian ones, the nonlocal magic grows linearly with the number $m$ of partially entangled fermion pairs. We show that this growth is an artifact of the Gaussian restriction: local Gaussian unitaries minimize the nonlocal stabilizer R\'enyi entropy for up to three pairs, but not from four pairs on. General local non-Gaussian unitaries that respect fermion parity take $m$ free-fermion pairs to fermionic Bell pairs with a fidelity that decays at most as $1/\sqrt m$ compared to exponential decay with Gaussian unitaries, so the nonlocal magic drops from linear to logarithmic in $m$. The reason is statistical --- Bell pairs have equal Schmidt weights, that is, a fully degenerate entanglement spectrum, and a state can stay far from them only if its Schmidt weights are spread over many orders of magnitude. This spread is measured by the capacity of entanglement $C_E$, the variance of the entanglement Hamiltonian, and the nonlocal magic of any fermionic state grows at most logarithmically with $C_E$. Free-fermion pairs add to $C_E$ independently, so $C_E$ grows only linearly in $m$, and this leads to the stabilizer fidelity decreasing at most as $1/\sqrt m$. Almost all the magic of free fermions, including Hartree--Fock and BCS mean-field states, is therefore local.

title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
authors: Abhijat Sarma, Ruochen Ma, Cenke Xu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07017v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability $p\in[0,1]$. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to $Sp(N)$ rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for $N\ge40$, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of $Sp(N)$ under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including $SU(N)$.

title: Single-shot ground-state preparation via strongly coupled baths
authors: Liang-Hong Mo, Jerome Lloyd, Yuxuan Zhang, Dmitry A. Abanin, Biao Lian
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07021v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Preparing ground and thermal states of quantum many-body systems is a central task in quantum simulation. Dissipative protocols have emerged as a promising solution for both near-term and fault-tolerant hardware, but most constructions rely on weak system-bath coupling, leading to slow cooling. Here, we construct cooling protocols at strong system-bath coupling, and demonstrate accurate state preparation within even a single cooling cycle. Our protocols combine dynamically ramped ancilla energy levels with time-dependent couplings to optimize the trade-off between cooling error and physical time. For a general class of free-fermion systems, we reduce the dynamics exactly to a two-level scattering problem: ground-state cooling becomes a control problem of maximizing resonant excitation transfer while suppressing non-adiabatic heating. We then construct a family of ``M\"obius-Ingham'' protocols, which reach optimal error scaling for gapless spectra and almost-exponential suppression of the leading heating error for gapped spectra, as a function of the cycle period. In our free-fermion benchmarks, M\"obius-Ingham cooling lies on the Pareto frontier between steady-state error and cooling time among the controls tested. We further demonstrate its effectiveness in interacting Ising and $t$-$V$ chains and the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Finally, we extend our construction to Gibbs state preparation, showing how free-fermion thermal states can be prepared in a single cycle.

title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
authors: Giuseppe Musolino, Daniele Lamberto, Salvatore Savasta, Federico Roccati
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07036v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase \pi/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.

title: Langmuir kinetics and totally asymmetric volume exclusion in linear chains via Fock space formalism
authors: Luis D. S. Silva, Arthur M. S. Carvalho, Francisco A. G. Almeida, Gerson C. Duarte-Filho
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07053v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Driven-diffusive systems combining spatial exclusion and bulk exchange, such as the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process coupled with Langmuir kinetics (TASEP-LK), serve as foundational models for particle transport in vehicular traffic, conveyor networks, and mesoscopic flow channels. In this work, we employ an exact Doi-Peliti field-theoretic operator formulation in Fock space to evaluate steady-state observables, continuous phase landscapes, and spatial correlations in finite linear chains up to $k = 16$. By introducing a decomposition in terms of biorthonormal eigenvectors for asymmetric non-Hermitian matrices, the stationary state is calculated directly from the kernel of the quasi-Hamiltonian, completely bypassing the computationally prohibitive complexity of full matrix diagonalization and time-dependent matrix exponentiation. Across distinct rate regimes and global parametric scans, our exact discrete calculations demonstrate that finite-size stochastic fluctuations naturally smear out singular domain walls, producing smooth density profiles and continuous phase crossovers. Finite-size scaling illustrates how local profiles systematically steepen toward the sharp domain wall predicted by continuum field theory as $k \to \infty$. Furthermore, two-point correlation analysis reveals that in slow-kinetics regimes, spatial fluctuations generate strong inter-site cumulants, causing standard mean-field approximations to systematically underestimate joint occupancy probabilities by 50\%. These findings emphasize the necessity of analytical methods for modeling mesoscopic transport systems and short traffic corridors where local stochastic fluctuations and spatial correlations dominate the stationary dynamics.

title: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
authors: Beg\"um Kabag\"oz
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07074v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Advanced LIGO is a gravitational-wave detector with extreme sensitivity, operating close to the quantum limits of optical measurement. The quantum noise in this system arises from vacuum fluctuations entering the interferometer readout port: phase-like fluctuations produce measurement imprecision, while amplitude-like fluctuations drive radiation-pressure back-action. In this review, we present an intuitive description in terms of complex fields and quadratures, and follow squeezed vacuum from its generation, through its interaction with the filter cavity and propagation through the interferometer, to the readout. We discuss how frequency-independent and frequency-dependent squeezing engineer quantum noise, and how correlations between optical quadratures map onto correlations between measurement imprecision and back-action. We conclude that LIGO is both a gravitational-wave observatory and a kilometre-scale platform for quantum measurement science.

title: Reliability of Fisher-information bounds for dielectric metalenses: a site-resolved RCWA audit
authors: J. Sumaya-Martinez, O. Olmos-Lopez
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07077v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We assess the reliability of localization precision predicted for a 1716-nanopillar dielectric metalens using a site-resolved complex RCWA library and a vectorial Poisson Fisher model. An independent calculation reproduces the archived local axial Cramer-Rao bound of 20.7738 nm to within 0.0044 nm, yielding 20.7695 nm under the same ideal detector and 3000 detected signal photons. High-order periodic-cell calculations reveal a 0.1335 rad phase difference at a selected diameter; different substrate-index assumptions prevent attributing this difference solely to modal truncation. Replacing the recalculated coefficients at 39 actual sites changes the bound to 20.7522 nm. Restricted phase-mask benchmarks and pixel-integration checks further distinguish a stable statistical prediction from electromagnetic convergence. We provide a reproducible, model-conditional benchmark, not a physical-device performance claim.

title: REST: Routing with En-route Seating Thresholds for pedestrian accessibility
authors: Nir Fulman, Himshikhar Mazumdar
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07095v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Public seating can support walking by providing opportunities to rest at useful positions along complete journeys. We introduce a route-based framework that assesses nearby seating, access to everyday destinations, and whether rests are well spaced along routes. One method finds the shortest route that does not exceed a chosen distance without rest; another allows longer stretches but adds a cost expressed as equivalent walking distance. We apply the framework to Mannheim, Germany. With a 1,000 m travel budget and a 500 m limit on walking without an opportunity to rest, 99.5% of older residents in Feudenheim lived within 500 m of a rest, yet only 33.5% could reach at least one destination in each of five categories (food shops, pharmacies, primary healthcare, public transport, and community services) on ordinary shortest routes meeting this limit. Finding alternative routes with sufficiently spaced rests increased this share to 61.4%; allowing longer stretches with an added cost raised it to 76.2%, compared with 89.7% when resting needs were ignored. Across Mannheim, 20.2% of older residents lost access to a reachable category when routes required a resting opportunity every 500 m, versus 7.1% when longer stretches were allowed at extra cost. Compared with the shortest physical distance, the least burdensome routes incurred extra costs from seating gaps: a median of 7.3 m of equivalent walking distance across city areas (90th percentile: 45.9 m). Better-placed seating could reduce this burden without changing street layouts. These measures help planners identify deficiencies, test improvements and guide route choices.

title: Particle-loss error correction using $2^l$-step states generated via particle-number-resolving measurement schemes
authors: S. B. Korolev, E. A. Nesterova
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07101v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an iterative scheme for generating finite superpositions of Fock states whose photon numbers differ by $2^l$ ($2^l$-step states). We derive an upper bound on the probability of generating such states. Based on the proposed class of states, we construct several bosonic encodings and compare their performance in correcting particle-loss errors. Our results identify the most efficient encoding, which achieves a higher channel fidelity than previously studied bosonic encodings.

title: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction
authors: Doyeol (David),  Ahn (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Newport Beach, California, USA)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07102v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sample-based quantum subspace methods construct a small subspace from measured basis states and solve the target problem classically within it. We study these methods for heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where the anisotropy $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp$ reaches $10^8$ to $10^{10}$. We prove two results for the energy-norm Galerkin solution. First, if the measurement basis is aligned with the flux surfaces and the subspace contains the poloidal-mode-zero block, the error is bounded by $\|r_0\|_{L^+}(\chi_\parallel-\chi_\perp)^{-1/2}$, where the numerator does not depend on $\chi_\parallel$. The bound is sharp, so the accuracy improves as the anisotropy grows. Second, in the computational basis, a subspace that misses a single node of a flux surface suppresses the flux-function component there as $\chi_\parallel^{-1/2}$, which gives an error floor when the limiting solution is nonzero on that surface. We verify both results on a shaped cross-section and on a KSTAR-like Miller equilibrium with ten qubits. At $\chi_\parallel/\chi_\perp=10^9$, the computational basis gives an error of order unity for every shot budget, whereas a quantum Fourier transform on the poloidal register gives $1.3\times10^{-5}$. The same barrier limits sample-based quantum diagonalization. The aligned measurement needs no time evolution, so the circuit is only state preparation and a five-qubit quantum Fourier transform. On a ten-qubit superconducting processor, the aligned basis gives a median error of $7.0\times10^{-6}$ with 768 shots, whereas the computational basis gives errors above 0.94 up to $1.2\times10^4$ shots. A trapped-ion processor shows the same behavior.

title: The lattice Boltzmann machine
authors: Hua-Dong Yao, Sauro Succi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07139v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The lattice Boltzmann (LB) method is widely regarded as a very flexible and efficient solver for a broad class of transport phenomena in fluids, soft matter and related fields. In this paper, we posit that such flexibility is a direct result of its generative nature as a rule-driven information-processing machine. Its update, a relaxation toward a local target followed by a shift along the lattice, belongs to the same class of iterated relaxation dynamics as residual networks and transformers, with the difference that in LB the operators are fixed by conservation and symmetry rather than learned from data. We show that three properties of this update are sufficient to promote the emergence of closed macroscopic laws from the underlying iteration process, the physical content of the target deciding the specific law in question. A machine whose target is drawn at random generates the transport law predicted from its moments. A network given the same three properties on a graph, where there is no lattice, is trained on a traffic process and generates a conservation law of its own. The mechanism has a precise limit, where the damping of the non-conserved modes fails, and on the lattice the macroscopic law gives no warning of it. In this reading, LB is a lattice Boltzmann machine whose informing rules are supplied by physics rather than by training. Its three properties then state what a new ingredient should preserve when it enters an LB model, whether it comes from physics or from data.

title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
authors: Zhengyu Cai, Mohamad Ali Jarkas, Bokun Zhao, Warren J. Gross
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07144v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce dithered belief-propagation decoding for circuit-level quantum memory to mitigate the oscillations and trapping behavior that limit standard belief-propagation (BP) decoders for qLDPC codes. Our approach combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation. Evaluated under circuit-level noise on the distance-11 rotated surface code and the distance-12 bivariate-bicycle code, the proposed dithered decoder significantly outperforms BP and BP+OSD+CS-10. The proposed decoder achieves accuracy comparable to or better than state-of-the-art Relay-BP, especially at higher physical error rates, while trading a moderate increase in additions for about 98% fewer multiplications on average and eliminating node-level RNGs. These results suggest that dithering is a promising approach toward real-time decoding of quantum memories.

title: Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations
authors: Alireza Maleki
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07153v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration. Our first key result is that geometric optimization is indispensable. For commonly assumed experimental parameters, neglecting the optimization of geometric ratios can suppress the accumulated phase, and hence the detectability of entanglement, by up to several orders of magnitude. Second, we provide a complete comparative analysis of two SG orientations (linear and parallel) and three MZ orientations (translation-symmetric, mirror-symmetric, and parallel-arms). The parallel-arms SG and MZ configurations tend to yield the largest phase accumulations and are nearly equivalent in performance, whereas the translation-symmetric MZ setup exhibits destructive-interference nulls that act as blind operating points where detection becomes ineffective. These observations highlight the importance of geometry-aware design. A Monte Carlo error analysis of realistic fabrication tolerances indicates that the parallel-arms configurations are generally more robust, maintaining low relative phase uncertainty over broad parameter intervals. Furthermore, an evaluation of Bell violations assesses the feasibility and signal-to-noise ratio of each configuration. Our results identify geometric optimization, particularly through parallel-arms designs, as an important consideration for near-term experiments targeting gravitationally induced entanglement.

title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
authors: Afonso Azenha, Ilia Polian, Sebastian Brandhofer
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising pathway to scale superconducting quantum hardware, but restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity creates a major transpilation bottleneck. Current DQC transpilation methods often assume idealized hardware connectivity, ignore subsequent intra-module routing, or suffer from substantial computational overheads that limit their applicability at scale. To address this, we introduce a scalable transpilation method tailored for the restricted connectivity of distributed superconducting quantum architectures. Specifically, our quantum interaction graph (QIG) approach couples a graph-partitioning mapping step with a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic. On a 48-qubit (3 QPUs $\times$ 16 qubits) architecture with all-to-all inter-core connectivity, our method reduces average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% (unstructured) and 24.01% (structured), while delivering >250$\times$ speed-ups for structured workloads compared to the state-of-the-art DMapS algorithm. On the 399-qubit (3$\times$133) IBM Flamingo, where DMapS times out on dense circuits, our approach maintains practical runtimes. Against a DQC-adapted SABRE baseline, it reduces structured circuit routing costs by up to 51.94% (all-to-all inter-core topology) and 51.96% (restricted line topology). Ultimately, this work delivers a practical transpilation method for DQC at scale.

title: Thermally-driven quantum reservoir computing
authors: Thiago Werlang, Daniel Valente
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07187v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Heat generation limits computation, classical and quantum, from single logic gates to entire data centers. However, an in principle limiting physical factor can sometimes be turned into a resource. In reservoir computing, energy dissipation is what gives a reservoir its fading memory. Here, we introduce a paradigm where the data injection itself is encoded on the time-dependent temperature of a thermal bath. We derive an exact expression for the nonlinear response of any fixed readout, and prove a rigorous memory-nonlinearity trade-off which turns out to be a structural necessity, rather than a tunable dynamical regime, since the same coupling that injects data also enforces equilibration. We illustrate both results with a driven qubit, using a single free parameter, and with a pair of coupled qubits, where the breaking of a discrete symmetry opens a fifteen-dimensional space to a single observable, yet that observable alone recovers just over half of it. This refutes the misconception that large Hilbert spaces guarantee computational power. Our results relocate the memory-nonlinearity trade-off from the reservoir's dynamics to its measurement channel, pointing to observable choice and bath engineering (instead of Hamiltonian control) as the physical levers for a thermally-native quantum reservoir computer.

title: Dispersive Corrections to Electromagnetic Energy and Power Flux Are Imprints of Eliminated Degrees of Freedom
authors: Stanislav Maslovski, Constantin Simovski
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a spatially dispersive medium the electromagnetic energy and flux are given by the frequency and wave-vector derivatives of the constitutive parameters, a result known as the Agranovich--Ginzburg (AG) formulas. Here, we clarify the physical meaning of the derivative terms in these relations and show that they measure the energy and flux carried by the degrees of freedom of the internal field-matter dynamics that the Maxwellian constitutive description hides. We construct an extended state-space model of such dynamics for a wide class of temporally and spatially dispersive media, from which the Maxwellian constitutive relations follow upon elimination of the internal variables, the effective material operator resulting from the Schur complement of the eliminated internal block. A congruence identity relates this complement to the extended state-space description, which allows us to extend the AG formulas to general bianisotropic media and to establish the conditions of their validity in the presence of dissipation. The AG dispersive corrections are thus the imprints of the eliminated degrees of freedom rather than independent constitutive postulates. They hold for fields driven at arbitrary real frequency and wave vector, and not only for eigenmodes, provided that the sources act on the fields alone and that any dissipation is carried by the electromagnetic subsystem. We verify the construction on the Lorentz, Drude, magnetized-plasma, and hydrodynamic models, the last of which describes a nonlocal metal. Additionally, a capacitively loaded wire medium is treated in the Supplemental Material.

title: Upper and lower bounds for few-copy Gaussian tomography, and the absence of a fermionic warm regime
authors: Ron Rubin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chen, Mele, Mele and Preskill proved a crossover for bosonic Gaussian tomography: cold states need $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies under single-copy or few-copy measurements, warm ones $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. The author proved $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ for adaptive single-copy tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states. This note shows the crossover has no fermionic counterpart and extends the fermionic bound to blocks of $k$ copies. There is no warm regime: on the quadratic Gibbs balls $\beta\|h\|_F\le\beta_0$ of unknown Hamiltonian $h$, the single-copy rate is $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ for every fixed $\beta_0>0$, at accuracies that resolve the ball, with a lower-bound constant independent of $\beta_0$. At the maximally mixed state a replicated-parameter Fisher budget gives $N>m^3/(8{,}553{,}600\,k\,\epsilon^2)$ for blocks of at most $k$ copies and all $\epsilon\le1/3600$; an exact formula for the maximal block Fisher information, via spinor tensor powers of $\mathfrak{so}(2m)$, shows that the budget $mt^2$ behind it is asymptotically attained for every fixed block size; whether $1/k$ is the true rate is open. Near the vacuum, block protocols need $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\min\{\sqrt k,m\}))$ copies, with no logarithm, via an exterior-power embedding of qudit tomography; parity superselection changes no rate, and number superselection costs nothing on number-conserving inputs. The embedding also carries upper bounds: a particle-number measurement followed by the $k$-copy qudit protocol of Nayak and Zhou attains the lower bound for every $k$ on number-conserving fermionic Gaussian states with bounded fugacity trace and on passive bosonic Gaussian states with bounded photon number, and a heterodyne stage that undoes displacement and squeezing extends this to all cold bosonic Gaussian states. This closes their $k$-entangled gap on the cold class; intermediate temperatures remain open.

title: Unifying First-Order Coherence, Concurrence, and Bell Correlations in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
authors: Bingbing Li, Tao Wu, Jiadong Shi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Neutrino oscillations provide a natural setting for investigating the quantum character of flavor conversion and the distribution of quantum resources over macroscopic distances. Here, we study exact relations among purity-based first-order coherence, pairwise concurrence, and the maximal Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) value in coherent three-flavor neutrino oscillations. By expressing the evolving neutrino as a three-qubit single-excitation state, we derive the generally mixed two-qubit reductions and show that the squared first-order coherence of each flavor mode and its two associated squared concurrences sum to unity. Furthermore, a closed two-branch relation is obtained, showing that the maximal CHSH value of any reduced pair is determined by its average first-order coherence and concurrence. The branch structure follows from the correlation-tensor spectrum and yields exact conditions for CHSH violation. For the vacuum parameters and propagation ranges considered, electron preparation gives weak CHSH violations in electroncontaining pairs, while muon preparation produces a dominant utau pair with substantially stronger concurrence and Bell correlations. The comparison also identifies the thirdflavor contribution responsible for the different locations of concurrence and CHSH maxima. These results clarify the distribution of quantum correlations during flavor evolution and provide a basis for extensions to coherent matter propagation and wave-packet-induced mixed states.

title: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schr\"odingerization
authors: Huner Fanchiotti, Carlos A. Garc\'ia Canal, Miguel A. Mayosky, Alejandro L. Veiga, Armando P\'erez, Rafael G\'omez-Lurbe, Vicente Vento
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The decomplexification procedure establishes a mathematical equivalence between finite dimensional quantum dynamics and classical dynamics by mapping the complex quantum domain onto the real classical one. Its inverse process, complexification --- which lifts a classical dynamics to an equivalent quantum formulation --- is of great interest, particularly because it enables the quantum simulation of equations that are of classical relevance. In this way, one can prepare the solution of classical differential equations to be implemented using quantum computation tools. In the present work, we recall the decomplexification procedure and also discuss several distinct strategies for performing the complexification of classical equations, so as to obtain the corresponding quantum-equivalent dynamics.

title: A componentwise spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann closure for finite-volume MHD at finite magnetic Reynolds number
authors: Min Ki Jung, Brian Wynne, Francisco Saenz, Yufan Xu, Yong-Su Na, Egemen Kolemen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07304v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: At finite magnetic Reynolds number, the field induced by a moving conducting fluid or solid extends into open space, so a finite mesh needs an outer boundary condition that represents the decaying exterior field. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) codes widely use pseudo-vacuum or truncation at a finite radius. Neither condition is physically correct for a vacuum exterior, but the exact alternatives are costly or limited to simple geometries. We present a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) closure on a fixed enclosing sphere and release it as part of the open-source multi-region finite-volume solver FreeMHD. The closure matches each Cartesian component of the vector potential to its decaying exterior solution, which retains all three decaying vector-Laplace families. A meshed vacuum buffer connects non-spherical conductors to the sphere. We verify the closure with manufactured modes, sphere free decay, sphere and oblate dynamos, and a freely braking rotor. Under refinement, oblate dynamo thresholds and sphere growth rates converge toward independent spectral references, and the rotor torque matches an exact transient reference. On the same sphere, pseudo-vacuum and truncation give the larger errors predicted by their exterior models.

title: A nonlinear interface for phase transduction
authors: Linshan Sun, Hao Zhang, Cameron Leary, Alex Amador, Sergio Carbajo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07316v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Broadband nonlinear frequency conversion mixes multiple input frequencies, complicating the transfer of programmed spectral phase between widely separated spectral bands. Here we identify and experimentally realize a quasi-linear phase-transduction regime enabled by broad phase-matching acceptance and effective localization of the complex frequency-mixing response. This selectivity can arise from coherent interference without narrowing the pump spectrum. We implement this regime through dispersive four-wave mixing in an argon-filled hollow-capillary fiber, transferring spectral phase from 1032-nm near-infrared signals to 344-nm ultraviolet idlers. Transient-grating frequency-resolved optical gating reveals frequency-inverted, phase-conjugating transfer of quadratic dispersion, localized phase steps, and low-frequency sinusoidal modulation. After correction for the modeled pump-induced phase background, the quadratic and step responses exhibit approximately linear point-by-point correlations. With increasing pump chirp, the transferred phase steps become more sharply preserved, and the fitted phase-transfer gains approach unity, consistent with enhanced effective localization. These results demonstrate quasi-linear spectral-phase transduction in a co-propagating broadband nonlinear interaction without spatially separating its spectral components.

title: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable
authors: Naoto Shiraishi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07337v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The frustration-free property is valuable in quantum many-body systems, which states that its ground states simultaneously minimize all local interaction terms, even when these terms act on overlapping degrees of freedom. Prominent examples include the AKLT model and Kitaev's toric code model, which serve as paradigmatic models of symmetry-protected topological phases and topological order, respectively. A fundamental question is whether a given Hamiltonian is frustration-free for all system sizes. Here we establish two seemingly contradictory results concerning this decision problem. First, we prove that frustration-freeness is decidable for any fixed local Hilbert space dimension. Specifically, there exists a finite, Hamiltonian-independent system-size cutoff such that frustration-freeness at this cutoff size guarantees frustration-freeness at all system sizes. Second, on the other hand, we also show that there exists a frustration-free Hamiltonian whose frustration-freeness cannot be proved within the standard axioms of mathematics (ZFC). We reconcile these seemingly contradictory results by showing that the cutoff, although finite for each local Hilbert space dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension. Our findings reveal an unexpected fundamental distinction between decidability and provability arising in quantum many-body physics.

title: Current frontiers in mobility and well-being
authors: Wen-Jing Li, Luo-Luo Jiang, Attila Szolnoki
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07343v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human mobility has a profound impact on social structure and collective behavior, which allows individuals to reshape group structures in response to strategy information, acting as a double-edged sword for cooperative behavior. It can both disrupt existing cooperative communities and enable individuals to escape adverse environments and seek high-quality interaction partners. This paper surveys current research progress on the impact of mobility on cooperation within the framework of evolutionary game theory, focusing on specific mechanisms of passive escape, dynamic self-organization driven by active choice, and the core trade-off between migration costs and speed. Mobility, an individual's spatial response to local strategic information that turns location into strategic advantage, influences cooperative evolution by altering interactive information and environmental feedback, consequently affecting sustainable social well-being, such as collective benefits. Under specific conditions, this self-interested behavior at the individual level can foster macrosocial harmony, embodying the unity of individual rationality and collective cooperation. Furthermore, we also discusses inter-layer migration and information routing mechanisms in multilayer networks and extends the perspective to human-machine hybrid systems where mobile agents with information regulation capabilities can serve as information supernodes. Our paper aims to provide a unified framework for understanding mobility as a combined physical and informational driving force in the evolution of cooperation.

title: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
authors: Dario Picozzi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07344v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Even a recovery that maximizes worst-input entanglement fidelity can retain avoidable errors in subsequent measurements. Entanglement fidelity is the probability of passing a test of whether the state and its entanglement were preserved; infidelity is the probability of failing it. Operational error is the largest possible change in any measurement probability, quantified by the normalized diamond distance. For every finite-dimensional noise channel and fixed encoding, we prove that operational error and worst-input entanglement infidelity have the same minimum over all recovery operations. The proof constructs one final unitary (a reversible quantum operation) that makes any recovery's operational error no greater than its original worst-input entanglement infidelity. With a retained noise record, we determine the optimal error and characterize all optimal decoders subject to a Kraus-rank limit for each outcome. For a fixed decoded channel, a semidefinite program finds the optimal final unitary in the low-error regime. We characterize all optimal final corrections and show that, at a fixed error floor $0<\epsilon<1$, the operational optimizers' sensitivity to residual unitary errors of size $s$ is at worst of order $s^{4/3}$, while the canonical polar correction has quadratic sensitivity.

title: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments
authors: Yongxi He, Xin Hong, Yu Luo, Xiangzhen Zhou, Shenggang Ying
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantifying the interactivity of quantum instruments is fundamental to understanding their resource structure and operational capabilities. Here, we introduce the interactive weight of quantum instruments as a resource quantifier that measures the minimum fraction of an instrument that cannot be explained by non-interactive components. Through quantum-information tasks including quantum-state recovery, positive linear loss games, and environment-assisted input-blind extraction, we establish quantitative bounds on the interactive weight of quantum instruments and exact operational characterizations of its complementary quantity, the maximal non-interactive content. In particular, we extend environment-assisted input-blind extraction to the setting of restricted environmental access and develop a corresponding framework. Within the allowed-operations framework introduced by Hsieh et al., we establish fundamental resource-theoretic properties of the interactive weight of quantum instruments, including faithfulness, convexity, and monotonicity under deterministic allowed operations. Furthermore, we prove that the maximal non-interactive content satisfies exact multiplicativity under independent parallel composition, yielding necessary constraints on multicopy resource conversion and establishing the finite-copy maximal-weight distillation no-go result under deterministic allowed operations. These results establish a unified theoretical framework for the interactive weight of quantum instruments from the perspectives of resource quantification, operational interpretation, and resource conversion, providing systematic theoretical tools for the quantitative comparison and conversion of interactive quantum instruments.

title: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Jing Tang, Junyu Su, Jie Chen, Ziyang Li, Yuangang Deng
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Controlling nonclassical light while maintaining a finite cavity response requires selective suppression of unwanted multiphoton excitation. We investigate a ring-cavity system containing two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, where electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) provides resonant access to a dark-state polariton. The exchange interaction shifts the polariton resonance while modifying the dressed two-photon excitation pathways. Strong photon antibunching emerges when the one-polariton resonance nearly coincides with a destructive-interference minimum of the second-photon transition amplitude. By jointly tuning the exchange interaction and control-field strength, pronounced photon blockade with a finite intracavity population can be sustained over an extended interaction range. We further show that the relative cavity-coupling phase redistributes optical coupling between symmetric and antisymmetric collective channels with opposite exchange shifts, allowing the photon statistics to switch between antibunching and bunching at fixed exchange strength. This mechanism provides a possible route to tunable nonclassical-light sources based on coherent control of collective excitation pathways.

title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
authors: Yusheng Zhao, Han Wang, Mingrui Jing, Zhongyi Ni, Xin Wang, Jie Wang, Jinguo Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07388v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $\Omega_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $\Omega_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.

title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
authors: Motohiko Ezawa
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07401v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.

title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
authors: Janarbek Yuanbek, Yuan-De Jin, Wen-Long Ma
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07404v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Weak value (WV) describes the amplified response of a meter when the measured system undergoes postselection. While conventional WV theory mainly rests on a single system-meter interaction setting, it remains unexplored whether WV can act as an effective pointer for sequential quantum measurements under postselection. Here we introduce the concept of WVs to the setting of sequential quantum measurements and quantum trajectories. We find that WV naturally emerges in postselected quantum trajectories of sequential weak measurements, by establishing a connection between the WV of the measured observable and the postselected statistics of quantum trajectories. Using sequential weak measurements on a qubit or an oscillator implemented by Ramsey interferometry with an ancilla qubit, we show that postselection shifts the collective record polarization away from the unconditioned ones, with an effective bias described by the WV. Our predictions are feasible to test in various platforms.

title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
authors: Xiao Liang, Takashi Yamakawa, Chak Fai Yung
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07413v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett-Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting. We establish the quantum analogue: if $\mathsf{UP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, then $\mathsf{NP}^{O}\cap\mathsf{coNP}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ with probability $1$ over a random oracle $O$.
  Beyond extending the classical result, this separation has a distinctly quantum significance: Shor's algorithms defeat canonical number-theoretic hardness candidates, while lattice assumptions and other leading post-quantum cryptographic assumptions do not directly supply hard languages with two-sided classical certification on every input. Our conditional oracle separation provides evidence that such structured quantum hardness can nevertheless arise from unstructured sources.
  Complementing this result, we rule out fully black-box quantum reductions of worst-case quantum hardness in $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ to post-quantum injective one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation. This barrier excludes a broad class of black-box approaches to deriving structured quantum hardness from generic cryptographic primitives, providing partial evidence that the non-black-box techniques in our first result are essential.

title: Information flow control in hybrid quantum networks
authors: Michael Siomau
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07440v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum resources can change the dynamical features and operational behaviors of conventional networks. Long-distance entanglement supports information transfer between nodes lacking a direct connection. This entanglement link not only modifies the stationary effective connectivity of the network but can also be used to suppress undesirable classical dynamics. By examining information flow control mechanism, we demonstrate that classical collective behavior can be well-balanced by altering the initially distributed entanglement. We show the entanglement thresholds for two distinct control approaches: linear response control and Lyapunov functional controllability.

title: Elimination of quantum causal confusion in the presence of dual states
authors: James Fullwood, Weixiang Ye
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07449v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: There is a rich class of bipartite quantum correlations between qubits which are consistent both with measurements performed in parallel and measurements performed in sequence. This phenomenon has recently been termed \emph{quantum causal confusion}, which is made mathematically precise by the notion of a dual state---a bipartite density operator whose associated correlations are causally ambiguous. A natural question is then whether or not the spatial and temporal scenarios associated with a dual state are fundamentally indistinguishable from a causal perspective. Here we show that as long as the reduced density operator of a dual state is oblique---meaning that all coefficients in its Pauli expansion are non-zero---then the underlying joint probabilities giving rise to such causally ambiguous correlations will differ in the spatial and temporal scenarios. Specifically, the temporal joint probabilities will inherently violate the no-signalling condition, thus eliminating quantum causal confusion. Moreover, as oblique states form an open dense subset of the Bloch ball, the elimination of quantum causal confusion is the norm rather than an exception.

title: Bell Test and Quantum State-Space Geometry
authors: Michael Siomau
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We explore a minimal phenomenological model of coupling between the geometry of the classical spacetime and the quantum state space. Assuming a simple structure of the combined manifold, bilinear interaction between the corresponding geometric scalars and the simplest case of the two-qubit entanglement dynamics, we derive an illustrative upper bound on the geometric coupling constant from the requirement of the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality violation over a finite time interval.

title: Stable dissipative topological solitons in media with even-order dispersion
authors: Xianan Sun, Dongdong Wang, Dumitru Mihalache, David Laroze, Boris A. Malomed, Pengfei Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07467v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The formation and dynamics of dissipative solitons are governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity, alongside the gain-loss balance. While it is known that dispersion orders beyond the conventional second order support stable solitons, the possibility of the creation of dissipative topological solitons in this setting was not explored. Here, we reveal a class of stable dissipative solitons enabled by the pure-high-even-order dispersion (PHEOD), with dispersion orders m=4, 6, 8, and 10. The resulting dissipative topological solitons (DTSs) and moving topological solitons (MTSs) are dark-type structures featuring a zero-amplitude point that separates two CW backgrounds with opposite signs. In particular, the PHEOD solitons feature oscillatory tails, which are not present in the conventional dark states. The linear-stability analysis confirms full robustness of the PHEOD-supported DTSs and MTSs. We also explore collision dynamics of MTSs, whose repulsive interactions are inelastic, leading either to rebound, accompanied by emission of dispersive radiation, or complete fusion. These findings establish PHEOD as a means for the generation of new species of dissipative solitons, and broaden the variety of nonlinear modes available to experimental studies in nonlinear optics.

title: Percolation of discorectangles oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions
authors: Yuri Yu. Tarasevich
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07484v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The percolation of finite-thickness elongated objects---discorectangles (stadiums)---oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions is studied, extending recent results for zero-thickness sticks. The angular distribution is the ``Maltese cross'' parametrized by $\alpha$. Based on the known analytic expression for the excluded area of a discorectangle pair, the percolation threshold is estimated by the eigenvalue method. The discorectangle connectivity matrix is represented as the stick matrix plus a rank-1 term determined by the constant part of the excluded area, $C=4lw+\pi w^{2}$, which gives the approximate relations $\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{DR}}\approx\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{stick}}+C$ and $n_c^{\mathrm{DR}}\approx n_c^{\mathrm{stick}}/(1+C n_c^{\mathrm{stick}})$. Finite thickness shifts the absolute thresholds and affects the first normalization, whereas the second normalization, written through maximum eigenvalues, cancels the additive geometric contribution and preserves only the orientational dependence, explaining the universality of the normalized curves. Monte Carlo simulations of unit-length discorectangles with aspect ratios 8, 16, and 32, various domain sizes, periodic boundary conditions, and union--find scaling analysis confirm the theoretical predictions.

title: Electrical conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium: discretization and effective medium approximation
authors: Yuri Yu. Tarasevich
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07491v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The effective conductivity of a two-dimensional two-component medium is studied within a discretization scheme and the effective-medium approximation (EMA). A square lattice is superimposed on a random isotropic medium; each cell is assigned the conductivity of its majority component, and the cell is replaced by a star of four resistors. Neighboring cells are connected by an equivalent resistor whose conductivity is $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$, or the harmonic mean $\sigma_{12}=2\sigma_1\sigma_2/(\sigma_1+\sigma_2)$, with probabilities $(1-p)^2$, $p^2$, and $2p(1-p)$, respectively. Applying Foster's theorem and the EMA yields a closed equation for the dimensionless effective conductivity $x$ and, after transformation, a cubic equation whose coefficients depend on $p$ and the conductivity ratio $r$. The EMA predictions are compared with direct calculations on a $200\times200$ resistor network with periodic lateral boundary conditions and Dirichlet conditions on the top and bottom. For uncorrelated disorder, good agreement is found. For correlated disorder, when resistor conductivities are assigned according to the discretization rule from the colors of adjacent nodes, significant deviations appear and the percolation-like inflection point shifts to the right of $1/2$. The results question the validity of the correlated-disorder EMA approach and help explain discrepancies previously reported for random nanowire networks.

title: Efficient Pauli Truncation from Operator Stabilizer R\'enyi Entropy
authors: Haihui Wang, Yongming Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Operator stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (OSE) quantifies the magic of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of their compressibility in the Pauli basis. We establish rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be efficiently approximated by Pauli truncation in terms of the scaling of its OSE. Specifically, we prove that volume-law scaling of OSE for $\alpha\geq1$ prevents efficient Pauli truncation from reproducing expectation values for all states at sufficiently small fixed error. On the other hand, logarithmic growth of OSE for $0<\alpha<1/2$ guarantees efficient Pauli truncation approximability uniformly over all states. A counterexample shows that this sufficient range cannot be extended on the basis of OSE scaling alone. If we restrict to correlations over suitable low-average state ensembles, then the sufficient range extends to $0<\alpha<1$. We further derive cumulative error bounds for iterative Pauli propagation and approximation guarantees for fixed-order out-of-time-ordered correlators. Moreover, under an independent-sign assumption, we show that logarithmic OSE for $0<\alpha<1$ guarantees efficient Pauli truncation with the prescribed accuracy for all input states with high probability. Our results provide a theoretical framework for understanding when operator magic constrains or enables efficient Pauli truncation and for guiding the development of classical simulation methods.

title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
authors: Mason Christiansen, Jae S. Hwang, Yi Jie Lin, Aryan Zaveri, Tianjun Li, Daniel Cui, Baolai Liang, Aaswath P. Raman
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. Here, we experimentally demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption in both polarizations at the same wavelengths and angles from a single structure, wherein a germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on a doped InAs layer scatters TE-polarized light into near fields with components perpendicular to the magnetic field, allowing the magneto-optic response of the InAs to act on them. Under a 0.48 T field from a permanent Halbach array, this structure exhibits a difference in absorptivity between $+B$ and $-B$ of 0.035 in both TE and TM polarization at 16.6 $\mu$m. Our approach shows that the magneto-optic response of a planar semiconductor and the resonances of a dielectric metasurface can be designed together, offering a potential route to dual-polarization nonreciprocity at fields available from permanent magnets for emerging energy and heat transfer technologies.

title: Optimal quantum metrology with restricted controls
authors: Li Sun, Haoze Wang, Chong Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07583v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum control can enhance sensing precision, but practical protocols are constrained by probe preparation and the available control resources. Optimizing the sensing protocol within these constraints helps establish what precision is experimentally attainable. We study quantum metrology from a fixed initial probe state under restricted Hamiltonian controls with bounded amplitudes. Building on Pontryagin's maximum principle, we formulate quantum Fisher information maximization at a prescribed interrogation time for multiple control channels subject to a weighted amplitude constraint. The formulation also accommodates stochastic Hamiltonian evolution and time-local master equations. A geometric description of sensitivity accumulation reveals the mechanisms underlying the optimized protocols. Two spin-$1/2$ examples demonstrate the resulting enhancement: time-dependent control outperforms optimized constant control in transverse-field sensing, while optimized waveforms improve upon CPMG pulses for AC-field sensing under strong colored noise. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing sensing protocols within available control resources to improve experimentally attainable precision.

title: Observing mixed-state Uhlmann winding numbers in integrated photonic quantum walks
authors: Baichu Yu, Qin-Qin Wang, Huilong Huang, Bin-Tong Yin, Xiao-Ye Xu, Feng Gao, Xin Wang, Keren Li, Sen Yang, Yuan-Yuan Zhao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Integer winding numbers provide a well-established classification of topological phases protected by chiral symmetry at zero temperature, but extending this classification to thermal mixed states remains challenging. The Uhlmann phase, a mixed-state extension of the Berry phase, provides a geometric framework for characterizing finite-temperature topology. However, this geometric phase is restricted to two quantized values and therefore cannot resolve the multiple thermal regimes associated with high winding numbers. Here, we experimentally observe integer mixed-state winding numbers in a photonic quantum-walk chip. We prepare and reconstruct thermal states associated with high-winding chiral Hamiltonians and their spectrum-preserving dimensional extensions. The reconstructed Uhlmann overlaps form closed trajectories in the complex plane, and their integer windings around the zero-overlap point are directly observed. As temperature increases, the Uhlmann winding number undergoes multiple discrete changes, accompanied by switches of the Uhlmann phase and the successive disappearance of momentum-resolved topological kinks. These results highlight an integer-valued topological characterization alongside the mixed-state geometric phase.

title: A Wigner-Lindblad phase space model for open quantum dynamics
authors: O. Morandi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07608v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate the collisional quantum dynamics of an open system in contact with a thermal bath. We propose a particle-bath interaction model based on the Weyl quantization principle and the Wigner phase space description of quantum evolution. By factorizing the reduced Hamiltonian of the open system via supersymmetric quantum mechanics techniques, we construct system-dependent creation and annihilation operators for arbitrary potential landscapes. This allows us to extend the classical Fokker--Planck relaxation mechanism to incorporate Lindblad quantum stochastic jumps within the Wigner phase-space formalism. Through a semiclassical expansion of the Moyal star product to second order, we obtain a generalized Wigner--Lindblad kinetic model featuring position-dependent friction and diffusion terms. We establish the mathematical well-posedness of the Lindblad problem and we validate our approach through numerical simulations. Our model resolves unphysical long-time artifacts of standard quantum Fokker--Planck models in quartic double-well traps, accurately captures dissipative quantum state localization in 2D molecular potentials (4D phase space), and effectively evaluates electron transport and trapping times in InAs/InP resonant tunneling diodes.

title: Evolutionary dynamics of collective-risk social dilemma game with risk uncertainty and adaptive strategy
authors: Chuanzhi Zhou, Ju Han, Xiaojie Chen, Attila Szolnoki
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The collective-risk dilemma game constitutes the leading metaphor for studying the evolution of cooperation in populations of selfish individuals. Although most theoretical studies often consider the risk level as a fixed parameter, this may not fully reflect the uncertain nature of risk detected in real-world scenarios. Motivated by the observation that individuals can infer their game environment and accordingly adjust their actual behavior, here we investigate this game with uncertain risk. In particular, we introduce a type of adaptive agents who incur an observation cost to infer the risk level during game interactions, and subsequently decide whether to cooperate or defect based on their tolerance thresholds. We first calculate the fixation probabilities of three different strategies in a mutation-free regime. Our results show that adaptive agents are favored by natural selection at low observation costs and moderate tolerance thresholds. Moreover, the fixation of adaptive agents results in higher levels of cooperation when both parameters are relatively low. We then consider behavioral mutation and systematically explore how average cooperation level and group achievement vary with observation costs, tolerance thresholds, and mutation rates. Importantly, the main results remain intact when the mutation is considered. Furthermore, when the tolerance threshold is small, the presence of adaptive agents results in a higher cooperation level and group achievement compared to the traditional setup when only unconditional cooperators and defectors are present. This advantage, however, gradually erodes with an increasing tolerance threshold and these two quantities fall below the levels observed in the classic two-strategy case.

title: Simulation of Refraction Through Voxel Volumes
authors: Rainier Mobley, Jean Michel L\'etang, Max Langer
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07690v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. We first validate this method compared to a model with an analytical solution, and then investigate the effects of voxel size, interpolation choice, and illumination to grid alignment on a few simulated test objects. From these investigations, we make several recommendations to guide simulations using these techniques.

title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
authors: Maria V. Ageeva, Denis S. Goldobin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07714v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

title: Separability and lower bounds of concurrence via symmetric measurement correlations
authors: Yuhang Xie, Yanjun Chu, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07727v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The detection and quantification of quantum entanglement is a central issue in quantum information science, particularly for unknown quantum states. Based on symmetric measurement correlation matrices, we present a family of separability criteria that can be experimentally applied without state tomography, and recover some related existing criteria as special cases. Using the constructed correlation matrices, we further derive a class of lower bounds of concurrence. Through illustrative examples, we demonstrate that our criteria outperform some existing separability criteria in entanglement detection, and that the obtained lower bounds on concurrence are tighter than known counterparts.

title: Unified design of short mode-evolution couplers
authors: S. -Y. Tseng
abstract:
arXiv:2611.07729v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Short mode-evolution couplers have been designed with several seemingly different approaches, including fast quasi-adiabatic dynamics (FAQUAD), counter-diabatic (CD) driving realized by tailoring waveguide widths and spacing, CD driving realized by axis bending, and numerical optimization of the coupler geometry. Using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers--Henneberger frame of the bent coupler, we show that these approaches belong to the same design space. The three geometric parameters, width difference, spacing, and axis tilt, act on the light through two functions only: the coupling strength, set by the spacing, and an effective detuning, set by the width difference and the axis curvature. The gauge, bent, and mixed realizations of a CD coupler are therefore the same device and have the same bandwidth. The bandwidth is set by the angle $\chi$ between the light and the field that steers it on the Bloch sphere, integrated along the device as $\int\sin^2\chi dz$, and for a CD coupler this integral is set by the reference alone. This leads to a lithography-aware design rule: make the reference as adiabatic as the minimum gap allows, by narrowing its spacing at the anticrossing, and let exact CD suppress the remaining nonadiabatic coupling. In beam propagation method (BPM) simulations on a polymer platform, a 500\um{} coupler designed this way, without numerical optimization, maintains ${>}99\%$ transfer over 274~nm at a minimum edge gap of 1.05\um, compared with 150~nm for the CD coupler of a fixed-spacing reference at nearly the same gap. Particle swarm optimization of the geometry with BPM in the loop does not exceed the design rule. Three-dimensional BPM of the BCB channel waveguides also confirms these conclusions.
